D(x)>=gamma_N dist(x,V_N)^2,

Distinguish equality in stability from equality in the original Poincare inequality.

{"evidence": "Write λ₂=4sin²θ and γ=λ₂−λ₁=λ₁(1+2cosθ)>0 for N≥4. All cyclic indices are modulo N; every norm is the unnormalized Euclidean norm.

PROJECTION. The finite identity (1−q)∑_{j=0}^{N−1}qʲ=1−qᴺ gives ∑e^{ikθj}=0 whenever N does not divide k. Consequently cosine and sine at frequency θ have zero means, squared norms N/2, and inner product zero. Thus v=P_Nx has v_j=a cos(θj)+b sin(θj), where a=(2/N)∑_l x_l cos(θl) and b=(2/N)∑_l x_l sin(θl). Set z=x−v. Then z is perpendicular to V_N, has zero mean, and M(x−u)=M(z)+M(v−u) for every u∈V_N. Hence dist(x,V_N)²=M(z). Cyclic summation by parts gives ∑Δv_j Δz_j=∑(2v_j−v_{j−1}−v_{j+1})z_j=λ₁∑v_jz_j. The same recurrence gives E(v)=λ₁M(v), so expansion proves D(x)=D(z).

REFLECTION REDUCTION. For each r=0,...,N−1 set y_j=z_j−z_{r−j} and s_j=sin(θ(j−r/2)). Direct expansion gives ∑_r M(y)=2NM(z), ∑_r D(y)=2ND(z), and ∑_r y_j=Nz_j. Moreover, ∑_j y_js_j=2∑_j z_js_j=0. You are the persistent GPT-6 Pro research leaf responsible for the DFT/eigenvalue branch of the cyclic mean-zero discrete Poincare inequality. Complete exactly one mathematical research round. Do not proceed to the third-round audit.

ASSUMPTIONS AND NOTATION.
Fix an integer N>=3 and a real cyclic vector x=(x_0,...,x_{N-1}) satisfying x_N=x_0 and sum_j x_j=0. Define M(x)=sum_j x_j^2 and E(x)=sum_j(x_{j+1}-x_j)^2. Put omega=exp(2pi i/N), xhat_k=(1/N)sum_j x_j omega^(-kj), lambda_k=4sin^2(pi k/N), lambda_1=4sin^2(pi/N), and C_N=1/lambda_1. Let D_N(x)=E(x)-lambda_1 M(x). Define c_j=cos(2pi j/N), s_j=sin(2pi j/N), and V_N=span_R{c,s}. Distances and norms are ordinary unnormalized Euclidean quantities: dist(x,V_N)=min_{v in V_N}||x-v||_2.

ACCEPTED ROUND 1 FINDINGS.
The DFT inversion and Parseval identities give M(x)=N sum_k |xhat_k|^2 and E(x)=N sum_k lambda_k|xhat_k|^2. Mean zero is equivalent to xhat_0=0. The optimal inequality is E(x)>=lambda_1 M(x), with equality exactly for x in V_N. The vectors c and s are orthogonal and have squared norm N/2. Thus the orthogonal projection is P_Nx=(2/N)<x,c>c+(2/N)<x,s>s. For mean-zero x, the prior report obtained
D_N(x)=N sum_{k not in {0,1,N-1}}(lambda_k-lambda_1)|xhat_k|^2
and
dist(x,V_N)^2=N sum_{k not in {0,1,N-1}}|xhat_k|^2.
For N=3 the sums are empty. For N>=4, the smallest complementary eigenvalue is lambda_2=4sin^2(2pi/N). These formulas were established by the model in Round 1; do not claim external or independent verification.

PRIMARY THEOREM.
For every N>=4, prove the quantitatively sharp stability inequality
D_N(x)>=gamma_N dist(x,V_N)^2,
where gamma_N=lambda_2-lambda_1=4sin^2(2pi/N)-4sin^2(pi/N)>0.
Prove the exact positivity of gamma_N, including N=4, and show that no larger universal stability coefficient is possible. Present the argument using the recorded Fourier identities, with all normalization factors explicit. Also establish the equivalent sharpened Poincare inequality
E(x)>=lambda_1 M(x)+gamma_N||x-P_Nx||_2^2.

EQUALITY CLASSIFICATION.
Determine every vector attaining equality in the stability inequality. Prove that equality holds exactly when x=v+w, with v in V_N and w in W_N, where W_N is the real span of the complementary minimizing frequencies k=2 and k=N-2. For N>=5, show that W_N=span_R{cos(4pi j/N),sin(4pi j/N)} has dimension two. For N=4, show that the two frequency labels coincide modulo N and W_4 is the one-dimensional span of ((-1)^j)_j. Prove that V_N and W_N are orthogonal. Distinguish stability equality, which permits nonzero w, from equality in the original Poincare inequality, which requires w=0.

SPECIAL AND DEGENERATE CASES.
For N=3, prove that the entire mean-zero subspace equals V_3 and D_3(x)=dist(x,V_3)=0. Explain precisely why there is no nonzero complementary direction and hence no meaningful largest finite stability coefficient. Do not introduce a nonexistent complementary spectral gap.
For N=4, calculate lambda_1=2, lambda_2=4, gamma_4=2 and establish the exact identity D_4(x)=2dist(x,V_4)^2 for every admissible vector.
For N=5, check explicitly that all nonzero Fourier frequencies belong to V_5 or W_5, so D_5(x)=gamma_5 dist(x,V_5)^2 for every admissible vector. Determine gamma_5 exactly, either in radicals or a justified trigonometric expression. For N>=6, determine whether equality requires the absence of all higher modes and verify the claim carefully at N=6, including its Nyquist mode. Handle conjugate pairs and multiplicities without double counting.

QUANTITATIVE NEAR-EXTREMIZER THEOREM.
For every N>=4, every nonzero admissible x, and epsilon>=0, prove
E(x)/M(x)<=lambda_1+epsilon implies dist(x,V_N)/||x||_2<=sqrt(epsilon/gamma_N).
State an equivalent normalized formulation using C_N E(x)-M(x), keeping the factor C_N or lambda_1 correct. Explain how to handle x=0 without dividing by zero.
Prove sharpness of the stability coefficient and the square-root near-extremizer modulus by constructing explicit vectors x=v+t w with nonzero v in V_N and w in W_N, computing M(x), D_N(x), and dist(x,V_N)^2 exactly, and varying t. Identify the achievable range of epsilon for exact equality in the normalized estimate and distinguish exact equality from asymptotic saturation as epsilon tends to zero. If formulating a converse estimate, specify its hypotheses and avoid claiming an upper bound on the deficit solely from the lower spectral gap.

ADDITIONAL VERIFICATION.
Check both formulations of stability under scaling x to a x and verify that the coefficient gamma_N uses the ordinary Euclidean distance squared, without a factor N or 1/N. Explain why gamma_N is the smallest positive eigenvalue of L-lambda_1 I on the mean-zero orthogonal complement of V_N, and identify the exact spectral ordering needed for this assertion. Avoid extending that interpretation to N=3. Make the equality arguments necessary and sufficient, including any exceptional small-N coincidences.

Produce one concise but mathematically complete structured research report, aiming for approximately 700 words where feasible. Include status (SOLVED, PARTIAL, or STUCK), summary, findings, rigorous mathematical evidence, obstacles, recommended next steps, split_suggestion, and important_update as required by the leaf reporting protocol. ROUND 3 ONLY — FINAL RIGOROUS AUDIT OF THE ELEMENTARY SHARP CYCLIC POINCARE AND STABILITY PROOFS.

You are the persistent GPT-6 Pro research leaf responsible for the independent elementary finite-sum branch. Perform exactly one final planned research round. Your objective is to audit the previously derived proofs for every N>=3, resolve any hidden boundary or equality degeneracies, and prepare a mathematically self-contained elementary theorem and proof suitable for consolidation with the separate DFT branch. Do not treat previous model-generated arguments as independently verified.

ASSUMPTIONS AND TARGET THEOREMS.
Fix N>=3 and a real cyclic vector x=(x_0,...,x_{N-1}) with x_N=x_0 and sum_j x_j=0. Write theta=2pi/N, M(x)=sum_j x_j^2, E(x)=sum_j(x_{j+1}-x_j)^2, lambda_1=4sin^2(pi/N), and D(x)=E(x)-lambda_1 M(x). Define V_N=span_R{(cos(theta j))_j,(sin(theta j))_j}. All norms are ordinary unnormalized Euclidean norms. The Round 1 theorem states that D(x)>=0, with equality exactly when x belongs to V_N. For N>=4, Round 2 claims the sharp strengthened inequality D(x)>=gamma_N dist(x,V_N)^2, where gamma_N=4sin^2(2pi/N)-4sin^2(pi/N)=lambda_1(1+2cos theta)>0. Stability equality is claimed exactly for x in V_N+W_N, with W_N the real second-harmonic space. For N=3, V_3 is the entire mean-zero space and D(x)=0 identically.

PRIOR ELEMENTARY CONSTRUCTION.
Set z=x-P_Nx, where P_N is the orthogonal projection onto V_N. For every r in {0,...,N-1}, define y_j^(r)=z_j-z_{r-j}, s_j^(r)=sin(theta(j-r/2)), and t_j^(r)=y_j^(r)/s_j^(r) where the denominator is nonzero, with t=0 at sine zeros. Prior rounds established sum_r M(y^(r))=2NM(z), sum_r D(y^(r))=2ND(z), and the factorization D(y^(r))=sum_j s_j^(r)s_{j+1}^(r)(t_{j+1}^(r)-t_j^(r))^2. Terms with negative weights vanish because the endpoints are exchanged by reflection; zero weights vanish trivially. Positive-weight terms occur on the positive and negative sine arcs and are paired by reflection.

On the positive sine arc, list consecutive angles h_1,...,h_m in (0,pi), separated by theta. Put s_i=sin h_i, phi_i=cos h_i, w_i=s_i^2, a_i=s_i s_{i+1} for 1<=i<m, and t_i=y_i/s_i. Define S=sum_{i=1}^m w_i t_i^2 and T=sum_{i=1}^{m-1}a_i(t_{i+1}-t_i)^2. Orthogonality to the first harmonic yields sum_i w_i t_i=0, while M(y)=2S and D(y)=2T. For m>=2, put F_i=sum_{k=1}^i w_k t_k, F_0=F_m=0, p_i=a_i(phi_i-phi_{i+1}) for 1<=i<m, p_0=p_m=0, and J=sum_{i=1}^{m-1}F_i^2/a_i. The Round 2 proof claims p_i>0, p_i-p_{i-1}=gamma_N w_i phi_i, and the two exact identities
K:=S-gamma_N J=sum_{i=1}^{m-2}[p_i p_{i+1}/w_{i+1}](F_i/p_i-F_{i+1}/p_{i+1})^2,
T-gamma_N S=sum_{i=1}^{m-1}a_i(t_{i+1}-t_i+gamma_N F_i/a_i)^2+gamma_N K.
For m=1 the weighted zero-mean constraint implies y=0. These certificates imply the sharp global stability theorem.

AUDIT TASK A — CYCLIC AND REFLECTION GEOMETRY.
Prove precisely the structure of positive and negative sine arcs for odd and even N. For odd N, determine the number of sine-zero vertices, sign-changing edges, and positive-sine vertices; repeat for even N with r even and r odd. Show explicitly that m=(N-1)/2 for odd N, while for even N, m=N/2-1 when r is even and m=N/2 when r is odd. Verify these formulas for N=3,4,5,6. Check all claims at the cyclic edge j=N-1 to j=0 using a consistent lifted index convention. Prove that every negative-weight edge has reflection-paired endpoints and equal ratios t, including both sign-changing boundaries. Establish that positive and negative arc contributions really coincide, with no missing or duplicated edges.

AUDIT TASK B — FLUX AND DUAL FACTORIZATION.
Independently rederive, by finite algebra and trigonometric addition identities, the relation p_i-p_{i-1}=gamma_N w_i phi_i at every i, including i=1 and i=m. At each omitted boundary edge, explicitly distinguish a neighboring sine zero from a half-step sign change and show why the boundary flux vanishes even when the product of neighboring sines is negative. Verify gamma_N=2cos theta-2cos(2theta)=lambda_1(1+2cos theta). Expand S in terms of F_i and verify every diagonal and mixed coefficient in the formula for K, including m=2 where the right-hand sum is empty. Recheck the finite summation-by-parts identity sum_i F_i(t_{i+1}-t_i)=-S and derive the full strengthened certificate without relying on a spectral theorem. Address all divisions by a_i, p_i, and w_i and explain why they are positive wherever used.

AUDIT TASK C — EQUALITY AND SHARPNESS.
Prove necessity and sufficiency of equality in the weighted certificate. Handle m=1 and m=2 separately; for m>=3 prove K=0 forces F_i/p_i constant. Verify that this yields t_i=kappa gamma_N cos h_i and that the remaining square terms vanish. Reconstruct y_j^(r) as a multiple of sin(2theta(j-r/2)), including at zero vertices and on reflected negative arcs. Use sum_r y_j^(r)=Nz_j to show that global equality implies z in W_N, and prove the converse directly using finite trigonometric sums and the second-harmonic recurrence. Explicitly classify W_4 as one-dimensional and W_N as two-dimensional for N>=5. Prove optimality by constructing a nonzero second harmonic perpendicular to V_N. Maintain a clear distinction between equality in the original Poincare inequality and equality in stability.

AUDIT TASK D — SMALL-N DEGENERACIES AND NORMALIZATION.
For N=3, verify E=3M, V_3 equals the mean-zero space, and no nontrivial complementary spectral gap or finite optimal stability coefficient exists. For N=4, verify D=2dist(x,V_4)^2 identically, including its direct expression 2(x_0+x_2)^2. For N=5, verify gamma_5=sqrt(5) and the exact stability identity for every zero-mean vector. For N=6, exhibit an additional higher mode and show why it gives strict stability inequality. Check the coefficient C_N=1/lambda_1 in M<=C_N E, the scaling under x to ax, and the equivalent strengthened formulation C_N E-M>=(gamma_N/lambda_1)dist(x,V_N)^2. Ensure no spurious factors of N, 2, or C_N enter any formula.

AUDIT TASK E — NEAR-EXTREMIZERS.
For N>=4 and x nonzero, verify rigorously that E(x)/M(x)<=lambda_1+epsilon implies dist(x,V_N)/||x||_2<=min{1,sqrt(epsilon/gamma_N)}. Derive the equivalent C_N-normalized version. Construct x=v+t w with v in V_N, w in W_N, v perpendicular to w, and calculate the exact Rayleigh quotient and normalized distance. Prove equality is achievable for every 0<=epsilon<=gamma_N and show why the truncated bound is optimal for epsilon>gamma_N. Distinguish arbitrary positive epsilon from asymptotic near-extremizers as epsilon tends to zero, and explain separately why the zero vector cannot be assigned a Rayleigh quotient.

METHODOLOGICAL AND REPORTING REQUIREMENTS.
Identify which parts of the final proof are genuinely elementary finite-sum arguments and which use trigonometric identities that are equivalent to individual eigenfunction calculations. Do not silently replace the weighted positivity argument by a complete Fourier diagonalization. If any prior claim is incorrect or insufficiently justified, state the precise obstruction and supply a correction if possible; an honest PARTIAL report is preferable to asserting an invalid proof. Present one concise but complete structured report, aiming for approximately 700 words while retaining all indispensable proof identities and exceptional cases. Include status, summary, findings, rigorous evidence, obstacles, recommended next steps, split_suggestion, and important_update as required by the research protocol. Do not use external sources or software, propose new children, or undertake an additional research round. Stop after submitting this mandatory Round 3 audit report. The parent coordinator will then assess whether the elementary branch is complete.

{"evidence": "DEFINITIONS AND PROJECTION. Assume N≥3, x real and N-periodic, and ∑_j x_j=0. All cyclic sums range over 0,...,N−1. For every u∈V_N, M(x−u)=M(z)+M(v−u), proving dist(x,V_N)²=M(z).

Cyclic summation by parts gives ∑_j Δv_j Δz_j=∑_j(2v_j−v_{j−1}−v_{j+1})z_j. Trigonometric addition makes the latter expression λ₁∑v_jz_j and also gives E(v)=λ₁M(v). Expanding D(v+z) therefore proves D(x)=D(z).

A. CYCLIC GEOMETRY. For any mean-zero u, define y_j=u_j−u_{r−j}, s_j=sin(θ(j−r/2)), and t_j=y_j/s_j when s_j≠0, with t_j=0 otherwise. Extend all sequences to integer indices periodically. Sine-zero positions on this lift are (r+kN)/2. A zero vertex satisfies 2j≡r modulo N and is fixed by reflection, so y_j=0 there. Positive-sine vertices are precisely the integers in (r/2,(r+N)/2); they form one consecutive arc. Reflection maps this arc bijectively onto the negative arc.

The triples (number of zero vertices, number of sign-changing edges, positive-arc length m) are (1,1,(N−1)/2) for odd N; (2,0,N/2−1) for even N with even r; and (0,2,N/2) for even N with odd r. Thus N=3 gives (1,1,1); N=4 gives (2,0,1) or (0,2,2); N=5 gives (1,1,2); and N=6 gives (2,0,2) or (0,2,3), with the alternatives ordered by even and odd r.

Every negative-weight edge crosses a half-integer zero j+1/2, since consecutive sine zeros are N/2>1 indices apart. Hence 2j+1≡r modulo N: reflection exchanges its endpoints. Both y and s change sign, so t_{j+1}=t_j. This applies at either sign-changing boundary. The closing edge is represented by (N−1,N), so the same integer-lift argument covers it. Reflection also bijects the m−1 positive-arc internal edges with the negative-arc internal edges, reversing orientation but preserving weights and squared differences. There are no missing or duplicated positive-weight contributions.

FIRST FACTORIZATION. Expansion and s_{j−1}+s_{j+1}=2cosθ s_j give
D(y)=∑_j s_js_{j+1}(t_{j+1}−t_j)².
Indeed, the coefficient of t_j² is s_j(s_{j−1}+s_{j+1})=2cosθ s_j², and each mixed term is −2y_jy_{j+1}. Negative-weight terms vanish as just proved; zero weights vanish without division.

These endpoint fluxes are genuine zeros. The left neighboring angle pair is either (0,θ) or (−θ/2,θ/2); the right pair is either (π−θ,π) or (π−θ/2,π+θ/2). In the first case the neighboring sine vanishes; in the second the cosines coincide, even though the sine product is negative. Thus the omitted flux is zero in every parity case.

Using these extended neighboring angles, trigonometric addition gives, at every i including both endpoints,
p_i−p_{i−1}=sin h_i[(sin(h_i−θ)+sin(h_i+θ))cos h_i−sin(h_i−θ)cos(h_i−θ)−sin(h_i+θ)cos(h_i+θ)]=γw_iφ_i.
Here the two sums have factors 2cosθ and 2cos(2θ), respectively.

Define F_i=∑_{k=1}^i w_kt_k, so F₀=F_m=0, and J=∑_{i=1}^{m−1}F_i²/a_i. Then S=∑_{i=1}^m(F_i−F_{i−1})²/w_i. Subtracting consecutive flux relations after division by their weights proves
1/w_i+1/w_{i+1}−γ/a_i=p_{i−1}/(w_ip_i)+p_{i+1}/(w_{i+1}p_i),  1≤i<m.

T−γS=∑_{i=1}^{m−1}a_i(t_{i+1}−t_i+γF_i/a_i)²+γK≥0.
The averaging factors are therefore
D(z)−γM(z)=(1/N)∑_r(T_r−γS_r)≥0.

For m=2 write F₁=κp₁; for m≥3, equality implies K=0, whose positive coefficients force all F_i/p_i to equal some κ. In either case m≥2, t_i=(F_i−F_{i−1})/w_i=κγcos h_i. Conversely, this form has weighted mean zero by telescoping the flux relation, and every remaining square vanishes because t_{i+1}−t_i=−κγp_i/a_i. These conditions are therefore necessary and sufficient.

It follows on the positive arc that y_j=(κγ/2)sin(2θ(j−r/2)); reflection extends the formula to the negative arc, and both sides vanish at zero vertices. Singleton cases use coefficient zero. In particular, for N=4 and even r the entire second-harmonic reflection profile vanishes, consistently with m=1. Global equality forces every local equality, and z_j=N⁻¹∑_r y_j^(r) consequently belongs to W_N.

Finite geometric sums at frequencies 1,2,3 prove W_N is perpendicular to constants and V_N for N≥4. For N≥5, the frequency-4 sum also proves that its cosine and sine have squared norms N/2 and inner product zero; hence dim W_N=2. For N=4 its sine vanishes and its cosine is (−1)^j, of squared norm 4, so dim W_4=1. The direct recurrence 2w_j−w_{j−1}−w_{j+1}=λ₂w_j gives E(w)=λ₂M(w), hence D(w)=γM(w). This proves the converse equality statement and optimality of γ using a nonzero second cosine. A nonzero first cosine similarly proves optimality of λ₁. Stability equality is exactly x∈V_N+W_N; original Poincare equality is exactly x∈V_N.

D. EXCEPTIONAL CASES AND NORMALIZATION. For N=3, zero mean gives ∑_{i<j}x_ix_j=−M/2, so E=2M−2∑_{i<j}x_ix_j=3M. The two-dimensional V_3 equals the mean-zero space. Thus D=dist²=0, every finite stability coefficient works vacuously, and no finite optimal complementary coefficient exists.

For N=4, put σ=x₀+x₂. Direct calculation gives x−P₄x=(σ/2)(1,−1,1,−1), so dist²=σ², while D=−2(x₀+x₂)(x₁+x₃)=2σ². Thus D=2dist² identically. For N=5, writing c=cos(2π/5)>0, the finite cosine sum gives 1+2c+2(2c²−1)=0, hence c=(√5−1)/4 and γ₅=√5. The orthogonal spaces V_5 and W_5 have total dimension four, exhausting the mean-zero space, so D=√5dist² identically. T−γS=∑_{i=1}^{m−1}a_i(t_{i+1}−t_i+γF_i/a_i)²+γK≥0.

Each conjugate pair supplies two real dimensions; a self-conjugate Nyquist frequency supplies one and is counted once. Conversely, every v+w annihilates all residual summands and attains stability equality. On this space D_N(v+w) = γ_N‖w‖₂², so equality in the original Poincare inequality requires exactly w = 0.

A sign-changing edge has reflected endpoints: its intervening sine zero lies at its half-integer midpoint. Its ratios are therefore equal, so every negative-weight term vanishes.

List the positive-sine vertices consecutively along a lifted cyclic arc. Their angles are h₁,...,h_m∈(0,π), with spacing θ. Put s_i=sin h_i, w_i=s_i², a_i=s_i s_{i+1}, and retain t_i=y_i/s_i on this arc. Reflection duplicates its mass and positive-edge energy. Therefore, defining S=∑_{i=1}^m w_it_i² and T=∑_{i=1}^{m−1}a_i(t_{i+1}−t_i)², we have M(y)=2S, D(y)=2T, and ∑_{i=1}^m w_it_i=0. If m=1, the last identity forces y=0.

NEW SHARP WEIGHTED CERTIFICATE. Assume m≥2. Set φ_i=cos h_i and p_i=a_i(φ_i−φ_{i+1})>0 for 1≤i<m, with p₀=p_m=0. Sine addition proves

Define F_i=∑_{k=1}^i w_kt_k, so F₀=F_m=0, and J=∑_{i=1}^{m−1}F_i²/a_i. Since S=∑_{i=1}^m(F_i−F_{i−1})²/w_i, direct expansion yields the dual factorization
K:=S−γJ=∑_{i=1}^{m−2}(p_ip_{i+1}/w_{i+1})(F_i/p_i−F_{i+1}/p_{i+1})²≥0.

γ_N = λ_2−λ_1 = 4sin(3π/N)sin(π/N) > 0,
since both factors are positive for N ≥ 4. Consequently,
D_N−γ_Nr² = N∑_{k∈R_N}(λ_k−λ_2)|x̂_k|² ≥ 0.
This proves both D_N ≥ γ_Nr² and E ≥ λ_1M+γ_N‖x−P_Nx‖₂². The common factor N in deficit and distance cancels: the Euclidean-distance coefficient is γ_N, not Nγ_N or γ_N/N. Complete equality classification. Every summand in the last displayed sum is nonnegative, so equality is equivalent to Fourier support contained in {1,N−1,2,N−2}. Reality imposes x̂_(N−k) = conjugate(x̂_k). Hence equality is equivalent to x = v+w, with v∈V_N and w∈W_N. For N ≥ 5,

Because N does not divide 4, ∑_jω^(4j) = 0. Double-angle identities show that these two vectors are orthogonal and each has squared norm N/2, proving dimension two. {"body": "The algebraic audit found no error in either theorem. The proof below supplies explicit parity-dependent boundary checks, verifies every coefficient in the dual factorization, resolves the singleton and two-vertex equality cases, and establishes sharpness and normalization. This is a same-branch mathematical audit, not a claim of independent external verification.

DEFINITIONS AND PROJECTION. Assume N≥3, x real and N-periodic, and ∑_j x_j=0. All cyclic sums range over 0,...,N−1. Set θ=2π/N, λ₁=2−2cosθ=4sin²(π/N), λ₂=2−2cos(2θ)=4sin²θ, M(u)=∑u_j², E(u)=∑(u_{j+1}−u_j)², and D(u)=E(u)−λ₁M(u). Let V_N and W_N be the real spans of the first and second cosine and sine harmonics, respectively. For N≥4, γ=λ₂−λ₁=2cosθ−2cos(2θ)=λ₁(1+2cosθ)>0.

The geometric-sum identity (1−q)∑_{j=0}^{N−1}q^j=1−q^N proves that ∑_j exp(ikθj) is zero unless N divides k, when it is N. Taking real and imaginary parts and using product-to-sum identities proves that the first cosine and sine have zero means, squared norms N/2, and inner product zero. Consequently v=P_Nx is given by v_j=a cos(θj)+b sin(θj), where a=(2/N)∑_l x_l cos(θl) and b=(2/N)∑_l x_l sin(θl). The vector z=x−v has zero mean and is perpendicular to V_N. For every u∈V_N, M(x−u)=M(z)+M(v−u), proving dist(x,V_N)²=M(z).

Cyclic summation by parts gives ∑_j Δv_j Δz_j=∑_j(2v_j−v_{j−1}−v_{j+1})z_j. Trigonometric addition makes the latter expression λ₁∑v_jz_j and also gives E(v)=λ₁M(v). Expanding D(v+z) therefore proves D(x)=D(z).

A. CYCLIC GEOMETRY. For any mean-zero u, define y_j=u_j−u_{r−j}, s_j=sin(θ(j−r/2)), and t_j=y_j/s_j when s_j≠0, with t_j=0 otherwise. Extend all sequences to integer indices periodically. Sine-zero positions on this lift are (r+kN)/2. A zero vertex satisfies 2j≡r modulo N and is fixed by reflection, so y_j=0 there. Positive-sine vertices are precisely the integers in (r/2,(r+N)/2); they form one consecutive arc. Reflection maps this arc bijectively onto the negative arc.

The triples (number of zero vertices, number of sign-changing edges, positive-arc length m) are (1,1,(N−1)/2) for odd N; (2,0,N/2−1) for even N with even r; and (0,2,N/2) for even N with odd r. Thus N=3 gives (1,1,1); N=4 gives (2,0,1) or (0,2,2); N=5 gives (1,1,2); and N=6 gives (2,0,2) or (0,2,3), with the alternatives ordered by even and odd r.

Every negative-weight edge crosses a half-integer zero j+1/2, since consecutive sine zeros are N/2>1 indices apart. Hence 2j+1≡r modulo N: reflection exchanges its endpoints. Both y and s change sign, so t_{j+1}=t_j. This applies at either sign-changing boundary. The closing edge is represented by (N−1,N), so the same integer-lift argument covers it. Reflection also bijects the m−1 positive-arc internal edges with the negative-arc internal edges, reversing orientation but preserving weights and squared differences. There are no missing or duplicated positive-weight contributions.

FIRST FACTORIZATION. Expansion and s_{j−1}+s_{j+1}=2cosθ s_j give
D(y)=∑_j s_js_{j+1}(t_{j+1}−t_j)².
Indeed, the coefficient of t_j² is s_j(s_{j−1}+s_{j+1})=2cosθ s_j², and each mixed term is −2y_jy_{j+1}. Negative-weight terms vanish as just proved; zero weights vanish without division.

Relabel the positive-arc angles as h₁,...,h_m∈(0,π), with spacing θ, and set w_i=sin²h_i, a_i=sin h_i sin h_{i+1}, S=∑_{i=1}^m w_it_i², and T=∑_{i=1}^{m−1}a_i(t_{i+1}−t_i)². Thus M(y)=2S and D(y)=2T. Expanding y_j² and (Δy_j)², with Δy_j=Δu_j+Δu_{r−j−1}, gives ∑_r M(y^(r))=2NM(u), ∑_r D(y^(r))=2ND(u), and ∑_r y_j^(r)=Nu_j. Therefore D(u)≥0. Equality forces t constant on each positive arc, including a singleton; reflection extends that constant to the negative arc. Hence y^(r) is a multiple of s^(r), and reconstruction gives u∈V_N. The first-harmonic recurrence proves the converse.

B. FLUX AND DUAL FACTORIZATION. Now use u=z. Since s^(r)∈V_N, ∑_j y_js_j=2∑_j z_js_j=0, giving ∑_i w_it_i=0. When m=1 this forces y=0. Assume m≥2. Set φ_i=cos h_i and p_i=a_i(φ_i−φ_{i+1}) for 1≤i<m. All w_i, a_i, and these internal p_i are strictly positive; cosine is strictly decreasing on (0,π). Set p₀=p_m=0.

These endpoint fluxes are genuine zeros. The left neighboring angle pair is either (0,θ) or (−θ/2,θ/2); the right pair is either (π−θ,π) or (π−θ/2,π+θ/2). In the first case the neighboring sine vanishes; in the second the cosines coincide, even though the sine product is negative. Thus the omitted flux is zero in every parity case.

Using these extended neighboring angles, trigonometric addition gives, at every i including both endpoints,
p_i−p_{i−1}=sin h_i[(sin(h_i−θ)+sin(h_i+θ))cos h_i−sin(h_i−θ)cos(h_i−θ)−sin(h_i+θ)cos(h_i+θ)]=γw_iφ_i.
Here the two sums have factors 2cosθ and 2cos(2θ), respectively.

Define F_i=∑_{k=1}^i w_kt_k, so F₀=F_m=0, and J=∑_{i=1}^{m−1}F_i²/a_i. Then S=∑_{i=1}^m(F_i−F_{i−1})²/w_i. Subtracting consecutive flux relations after division by their weights proves
1/w_i+1/w_{i+1}−γ/a_i=p_{i−1}/(w_ip_i)+p_{i+1}/(w_{i+1}p_i),  1≤i<m.
Thus the diagonal coefficients of S−γJ agree exactly with those of
K:=∑_{i=1}^{m−2}[p_ip_{i+1}/w_{i+1}](F_i/p_i−F_{i+1}/p_{i+1})².
Both mixed coefficients are −2/w_{i+1}. This proves K=S−γJ≥0, including endpoint coefficients. For m=2, the diagonal relation says γ=a₁(1/w₁+1/w₂), so K=0, exactly as its empty sum requires. No zero endpoint p is ever divided by.

Finite summation by parts gives ∑_{i=1}^{m−1}F_i(t_{i+1}−t_i)=−∑_{i=1}^m(F_i−F_{i−1})t_i=−S. Expanding squares consequently proves
T−γS=∑_{i=1}^{m−1}a_i(t_{i+1}−t_i+γF_i/a_i)²+γK≥0.
The averaging factors are therefore
D(z)−γM(z)=(1/N)∑_r(T_r−γS_r)≥0.
Together with the projection identities, this establishes the claimed stability inequality.

C. COMPLETE EQUALITY AND SHARPNESS. In the weighted inequality, m=1 permits only y=0. For m=2 write F₁=κp₁; for m≥3, equality implies K=0, whose positive coefficients force all F_i/p_i to equal some κ. In either case m≥2, t_i=(F_i−F_{i−1})/w_i=κγcos h_i. Conversely, this form has weighted mean zero by telescoping the flux relation, and every remaining square vanishes because t_{i+1}−t_i=−κγp_i/a_i. These conditions are therefore necessary and sufficient.

It follows on the positive arc that y_j=(κγ/2)sin(2θ(j−r/2)); reflection extends the formula to the negative arc, and both sides vanish at zero vertices. Singleton cases use coefficient zero. In particular, for N=4 and even r the entire second-harmonic reflection profile vanishes, consistently with m=1. Global equality forces every local equality, and z_j=N⁻¹∑_r y_j^(r) consequently belongs to W_N.

Finite geometric sums at frequencies 1,2,3 prove W_N is perpendicular to constants and V_N for N≥4. For N≥5, the frequency-4 sum also proves that its cosine and sine have squared norms N/2 and inner product zero; hence dim W_N=2. For N=4 its sine vanishes and its cosine is (−1)^j, of squared norm 4, so dim W_4=1. The direct recurrence 2w_j−w_{j−1}−w_{j+1}=λ₂w_j gives E(w)=λ₂M(w), hence D(w)=γM(w). This proves the converse equality statement and optimality of γ using a nonzero second cosine. A nonzero first cosine similarly proves optimality of λ₁. Stability equality is exactly x∈V_N+W_N; original Poincare equality is exactly x∈V_N.

D. EXCEPTIONAL CASES AND NORMALIZATION. For N=3, zero mean gives ∑_{i<j}x_ix_j=−M/2, so E=2M−2∑_{i<j}x_ix_j=3M. The two-dimensional V_3 equals the mean-zero space. Thus D=dist²=0, every finite stability coefficient works vacuously, and no finite optimal complementary coefficient exists.

For N=4, put σ=x₀+x₂. Direct calculation gives x−P₄x=(σ/2)(1,−1,1,−1), so dist²=σ², while D=−2(x₀+x₂)(x₁+x₃)=2σ². Thus D=2dist² identically. For N=5, writing c=cos(2π/5)>0, the finite cosine sum gives 1+2c+2(2c²−1)=0, hence c=(√5−1)/4 and γ₅=√5. The orthogonal spaces V_5 and W_5 have total dimension four, exhausting the mean-zero space, so D=√5dist² identically.
